findings.source_passage: these naked Nantucketers, these sea hermits, issuing from their ant-hill in the sea, overrun and conquered the watery world like so many Alexanders; parcelling out among them the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian oceans, as the three pirate powers did Poland
findings.why_it_matters: The Alexander/Poland analogy is one of the chapter's most rhetorically distinctive and critically cited passages; its complete absence erases a signature geopolitical-imperial conceit that defines the chapter's interpretive argument about Nantucketer sovereignty.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'like so many Alexanders' sentence and the Poland comparison verbatim or near-verbatim; this is the rhetorical hinge of the chapter's climax.

findings.source_passage: Look now at the wondrous traditional story of how this island was settled by the red-men. Thus goes the legend.
findings.why_it_matters: The ceremonious framing ('Look now,' 'Thus goes the legend') is voice-establishing and sets the narrative as oral/mythic; the draft collapses it to a flat 'The old legend says,' erasing the rhetorical register.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'Look now at the wondrous traditional story' and 'Thus goes the legend' as the paragraph opener.

findings.source_passage: most monstrous and most mountainous! That Himmalehan, salt-sea Mastodon, clothed with such portentousness of unconscious power, that his very panics are more to be dreaded than his most fearless and malicious assaults!
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamatory elaboration on the Mastodon ('clothed with such portentousness of unconscious power… very panics more to be dreaded') is rhythmically and thematically distinctive; the draft retains only the label 'Himmalehan, salt-sea Mastodon' and drops the entire interpretive expansion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full elaboration on the Mastodon's unconscious power and the fear of its panics, at least as a compressed clause.

findings.source_passage: Take out your map and look at it. See what a real corner of the world it occupies; how it stands there, away off shore, more lonely than the Eddystone lighthouse.
findings.why_it_matters: The imperative address ('Take out your map') is the chapter's voice-defining direct-reader gesture; the draft drops it entirely, beginning instead with a noun phrase, losing the characteristic Ishmael rhetorical mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the Nantucket description with 'Take out your map and look at it' to preserve the direct-address voice.

findings.source_passage: There is more sand there than you would use in twenty years as a substitute for blotting paper. Some gamesome wights will tell you… that one blade of grass makes an oasis, three blades in a day's walk a prairie
findings.why_it_matters: The extended satirical list of extravaganzas ('blotting paper,' 'Canada thistles,' 'toadstools,' 'oasis/prairie,' 'quicksand shoes') is a signature comic passage; the draft radically abbreviates it to three items, losing nearly all the ironic accumulation that earns the punchline 'Nantucket is no Illinois.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore most of the list items—blotting-paper sand, Canada thistles, spile-beyond-seas, wood-as-true-cross, toadstools, oasis/prairie—to preserve the satirical voice and earn the concluding line.

findings.source_passage: he hides among the waves, he climbs them as chamois hunters climb the Alps
findings.why_it_matters: The chamois-hunter simile adds lyrical texture to the paragraph's extended portrait of the Nantucketer at sea; its omission slightly thins the concluding set-piece.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the chamois-hunter comparison before the gull simile.

summary: The draft commits one high-severity loss (the Alexander/Poland passage, a critically signature analogy) and four medium-severity flattening failures spanning the imperatives, the comic extravaganza list, the Mastodon elaboration, and the Nantucketer-as-Alexander framing, cumulatively gutting the chapter's rhetorical and satirical character.
